subject: Regional reliability & residency: pinning scope and 3P onboarding
body:
Message 1
From: Alex Moreno <alex@nimbushealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Regional reliability and residency: pinning scope & third-party onboarding

Hi Jordan —

Quick one as we kick legal/ops review on Redwood: Nimbus needs written confirmation of the following before we can sign the Dedicated commitment. Can you confirm or clarify: 

1) Primary residency: can customer workloads be pinned to EU (Frankfurt) for both inference and logs?
2) Failover carveout: what is the maximum transient cross-region processing window you allow for capacity failover (hours/days)?
3) KMS: do you support customer-managed keys for EU-pinned workloads, and are keys held in EU?
4) Subprocessor onboarding: we need a roster with planned activation dates for any non-Redwood subprocessors that will process EU traffic within the next 12 months.
5) Evidence: sample audit logs retention policy and SOC 2 evidence timeline.

We’re aiming to close procurement next week; if you can share a short playbook + timelines and a proposed DPA addendum we’ll route to our legal ops.

Thanks,
Alex
Director, Cloud Ops
NimbusHealth
(attachment: NimbusLegal_questions.pdf)

----
Message 2
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Alex Moreno <alex@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 11:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Regional reliability and residency: pinning scope & third-party onboarding

Alex — thanks for the clear list. High level answers and next steps below; I included Marissa and Karthik for DPA/ops details.

Summary answers:
- Residency: yes — we can operate primary processing and access logs from our EU region (Frankfurt) for your tenant.
- Failover carveout: standard: ephemeral cross-region failover allowed for up to 72 hours in response to connectivity or capacity outages; longer windows require a documented exception and notification.
- KMS: we support customer-managed keys (BYOK) via our KMS integrations; keys can be provisioned in EU and bound to the tenant’s blob. KMS invocation stays in-region unless exception triggers.
- Subprocessors: we will provide the current roster and a 90-day activation notice for planned subprocessors.
- Evidence: SOC 2 report available; audit log retention default is 12 months (configurable up to 24 months on Dedicated).

Attachments: regional-pinplaybook-v1.pdf (playbook outline), subprocessor_timeline.csv (planned activations).

Next steps I propose:
1) Marissa will circulate a DPA addendum draft (incorporates BYOK and failover carveout language).
2) We’ll provide the subprocessor roster + activation schedule within 48 hours.
3) Ops (Karthik) will follow up with the technical runbook and IP/eRegion lists.

If that timeline works I’ll set a 30-minute sync with your security ops Monday.

— Jordan
Senior Partnerships Manager
Redwood Inference
(attachment: regional-pinplaybook-v1.pdf)

----
Message 3
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Moreno <alex@nimbushealth.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 14:20:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Regional reliability and residency: pinning scope & third-party onboarding

Alex — looping legal/ops questions into one place. I’ve attached a DPA addendum draft that captures: EU residency obligation, transient failover carveout (72h default), BYOK obligations, and audit log retention. Please review and mark any clauses your counsel would like adjusted.

A few clarifying notes up front: 
- The 72-hour window is for emergency capacity/recovery only; we log all transient processing events and notify customers when the exception is used.
- We will provide a subprocessor roster as an exportable CSV and maintain a 90-day notification cadence for any changes.
- SOC 2: we can share the most recent report under an NDA if required; standard turn is 3 business days for delivery to legal teams once the NDA is in place.

(attachment: DPA-addendum-draft.docx)

Marissa Cole
Head of Legal Ops, Redwood Inference

----
Message 4
From: Nimbus Legal <legal@nimbushealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 16 May 2027 08:45:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Regional reliability and residency: pinning scope & third-party onboarding

Marissa/Jordan — thank you. A few legal ops asks from our side after a quick review of the addendum: 

1) Evidence of in-region KMS key residency: can you confirm KMS provider and that key material never leaves EU control plane?
2) Audit log schema: please provide sample log entries showing the fields and retention metadata.
3) IP allowlist: we need the egress IPs/URL endpoints that will appear in outbound telemetry during failover.
4) DocuSign: please send your standard addendum for signature and supply a HubSpot/DocuSign link.

Attached: NimbusLegal_questions.pdf — we've annotated a few clauses.

Regards,
R. Singh
Senior Counsel, NimbusHealth
(attachment: NimbusLegal_questions.pdf)

----
Message 5
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: R. Singh <legal@nimbushealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 16 May 2027 10:30:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Regional reliability and residency: pinning scope & third-party onboarding

R — quick ops-level answers and links below. Happy to jump on the Monday sync for deeper tech review.

- KMS provider & residency: we support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS (multi-account BYOK) and Azure Key Vault. For EU-pin customers we recommend provisioning keys in the EU region (eu-central-1 / West Europe). Key material never leaves the customer-managed key service region; Redwood stores only wrapped key handles.

- Audit log schema (sample): timestamp, tenant_id, request_id, model_id, region, action, source_ip, egress_region, transient_flag. Example entry included inline below. Retention default 12 months (configurable).

  2027-05-15T11:01:23Z, tenant=NH-3281, req=abcd1234, model=gpt-3.x, region=eu-central-1, action=generate, src_ip=203.0.113.45, egress_region=eu-central-1, transient_flag=false

- IPs/endpoints during failover: we publish a scoped list of egress IP ranges per region; for now we can provide a CSV of the specific ranges used by the EU failover cluster and a short-lived allowlist that will be valid for 7 days ahead of the planned go-live.

- KV & cache: we do not persist customer KV cache to secondary regions; during a failover we rehydrate from encrypted exchange or fall back to cold-start behavior depending on model configuration.

- Runbook / telemetry: see runbook stub (attachment) for the notification cadence (email + API webhook), telemetry fields, and post-failover replay checks.

Attachments: failover-runbook-stub.txt (ops stub)

Karthik Iyer
Principal Engineer, Regional Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

----
Follow-ups pending: Marissa to push finalized DPA addendum + DocuSign link; Jordan to schedule Monday security/ops sync with Nimbus; Karthik to push IP list and full runbook during the sync.
